settings.heading: Turn Your Greek Yogurt Around and Read the Back
settings.standfirst: Same shelf. Same price. Nearly twice the protein. Why the cup in your fridge is quietly underdelivering, and what to look for on the back.
settings.caption: The back of the cup, not the front. Both panels photographed on the same shelf, Lagos, Month 2026.

settings.lead: You made the right decision already.
settings.body_before:
You skipped the sugary drinking yogurts. You went to the shelf with the thick Greek-style cups, the ones with the clean packaging and the word Greek on the front, and you paid ₦5,500 for one because you're trying to eat more protein and this seemed like the sensible way to do it.

That was a good call. It's just that you're getting less for it than you think.

Turn the cup around. Find the nutrition panel. Look at protein per 100g.
settings.stat_label: Protein per 100g on most cups on that shelf
settings.body_after:
On a 400g cup, that's 30 to 40 grams of protein for your ₦5,500.

Which is fine. It's just not what you're paying for.

settings.heading: Here's the same shelf, priced honestly.
settings.note: Real shelf prices and real panels, photographed the week of launch. If a brand's numbers beat the assumption, it goes in anyway.
settings.delta_heading: Same price. Same size cup. More protein.
settings.delta_body: Over a week of one cup a day, that gap is 133g of protein you either got or didn't, for identical money.

settings.lead: It isn't that the other brands are cutting corners. It's that they're not built for this.
settings.body:
Greek-style yogurt is a dairy product that happens to have decent protein. It is formulated for texture and taste first, and the protein figure is whatever the recipe leaves behind. Nobody on that shelf was optimising for it, so nobody prints it on the front.

Retaur was built the other way round: the protein figure first, then the recipe that hits it. It is the first sports nutrition brand manufactured in Nigeria. Formulated for the number, produced and tested in Lagos, priced to sit on the same shelf.
settings.footnote: Measured from the finished product, not calculated from a recipe. No fillers.

settings.question: “Does 54g taste like chalk?”
settings.answer: No. Reviewers reach for the Greek comparison on their own: as thick as Greek yoghurt, creamy, filling without feeling heavy, better frozen. It is not perfect. There is no unsweetened option yet, and one reviewer thought the pack was smaller than expected. Both of those are fair.

settings.question: “Is 54g even real?”
settings.answer: It is measured, not estimated. Protein base sourced from supplier line as you want to disclose it, produced and tested here, which is why 13.6g per 100g is a lab result on the actual cup rather than a figure copied off a supplier spec sheet. NAFDAC registration no.
